Classification: Public 
Aerial Wildlife Survey Report 
Wildlife Management Unit 308 Aerial Ungulate Survey (2025) 
Background 
WMU 308 is located in southwest, Alberta. It is 
bordered by highways 22 and 532, the Maycroft Road 
on the south and the Kananaskis road on the west. It 
consists of foothills and mountain habitats. WMU 308 
has good quality habitat for moose, elk, and mule 
deer. WMU 308 was also surveyed specifically for elk 
in 2007,2015 and 2020. Past surveys did not calculate 
population densities or estimates for deer species or 
moose. 
Survey Method 
A rotary wing (Astar-B3) transect survey was 
conducted February 13, 2025 flying 33 east-west lines 
at 1.85 km intervals, with 48 per cent coverage (800 m 
wide survey strip, area surveyed 282.8 km2) for a total 
linear survey effort of 353.5 km. At each observation 
point, ungulates were classified by species, and when 
possible, sex and age were recorded.  
Because transects varied in length, the average 
density (R) of mule deer, white-tailed deer, and moose 
was calculated by multiplying the number of animals 
per transect (Σx) by total area searched (total survey 
strip area [Σz]) (Jolly 1969, as described in Krebs 
2014). Average density (R) was multiplied by the area 
(km2) of the WMU (Z) to determine population 
estimates with a 90 per cent confidence intervals. 
Confidence interval width was calculated by 
multiplying the t statistic for the left-tailed inverse of the 
Student’s t-distribution, (t0.05,df=n-1) by standard error 
(SE; without replacement) of the abundance estimate 
where SE = sq root variance and variance = N*(N-n)/ 
(n*(n-1))*(Σx2+R2*ΣZ2-2*R*Σxz)  with N as the total 
number of possible transects given 100 per cent 
coverage, and n as the number of transects sampled.  
Moose, deer and elk observations made during the 
survey were recorded even if outside of the transect 
width. Moose, mule deer and white-tailed deer data 
points were truncated to 800m strip width for 
population estimates. All elk observations were 
summed for a minimum total count.   
Results 
Mule Deer 
A total of 195 mule deer were observed on transect 
with an average group size of 6.7 (range 1-31). The 
estimated density was 0.69 mule deer/km2 and the 
estimated abundance was 451 individuals (90 per cent 
CI 274 – 629). A total of 188 mule deer were 
successfully classified and the buck:doe:fawn ratio 
was calculated to be 48:100:48. Due to the timing of 
the survey being mid-February, a small amount of 
antler drop had occurred which will affect these ratios.  
White-tailed Deer 
A total of 319 white-tailed deer were observed on 
transect with an average group size of 4.5 (range 1-
14). The estimated density was 1.13 deer/km2 and the 
estimated abundance was 738 individuals (90 per cent 
CI 545-931). White-tailed deer were not classified into 
sex and age cohorts due to extensive antler drop 
having occurred by the time the survey was 
conducted. The 2025 population estimate represents 
the only statistically rigorous method employed for 
white-tailed deer in WMU 308.  
Moose 
A total of 75 moose were observed on transect with 
and average group size of 1.77 (range 1-3). The 
estimated density was 0.27 moose/ km2 and the 
estimated abundance was 174 individuals (90 per cent 
CI 117-230). The bull:cow:calf ratio was found to be 
38:100:45. Moose were generally counted anecdotally 
in past surveys for a minimum total count, which likely 
greatly underestimated the population. 
Elk 
A
 total of 328 elk were observed with an average 
group size of 59 (range 1-242). The bull:cow:calf ratio 
was found to be 10:100:20. The past surveys are 
presented in Table 1. The elk population in 2025 is 
11% lower than that reported in 2020.
